research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Highlights the work of the Innocence Project in securing DNA testing that proved Maher's innocence in multiple sexual assault cases after 19 years. Available via NBC/Peacock.
research_notes_other.research_findings: Dennis Maher, a US Army sergeant, was convicted based on misidentifications by multiple victims. The New England Innocence Project took his case, and crucial biological evidence, previously thought lost, was discovered in a courthouse basement in 2001. DNA testing excluded Maher, leading to his exoneration in 2003. His case also involved allegations of police misconduct regarding a deal with a witness. While the specific Dateline episode "Window of Hope" wasn't confirmed, the details align with the description.

contributing_factors_raw: Mistaken eyewitness identification (by multiple victims), failure to test biological evidence pre-trial, alleged police misconduct (withholding evidence about a deal with one victim/witness)
featured_individuals.status_raw: Exonerated by DNA evidence found years later; Received state compensation and settled federal civil rights lawsuit
organizations_involved_raw: New England Innocence Project (NEIP); Innocence Project (initial contact)
